title: Throughput to Hire — Price Sensitivity Pocket Guide
content:
One-pager / pocket guide for on-call pricing + hire triggers when throughput changes or latency targets shift. Intended for finance on-call, SRE/ops leads, and product owners.

Summary:
- Objective: convert throughput/latency stress signals into clear, operational pricing and hiring triggers that protect runway while preserving SLAs.
- Audience: finance on-call, ops lead, product manager for Dedicated.
- Status: experiment/proof-of-concept; use for next 90d ops playbook.

Assumptions (baseline):
- Baseline token cost (weighted mix): $0.00032 per token served (mix of embeddings + gen).
- Average customer request tokens/session: 420 tokens.
- Baseline sustained throughput (global): 150M tokens/day.
- Median time-to-fill engineer hire (backend/gpu infra): 10 weeks.
- Avg fully-loaded cost per hire (first-year): $180,000.
- Target latency SLO for PL1 routes: 120ms p95.

Quick reference scenario table (illustrative):
Scenario, 30d token uplift %, incremental tokens/day, incremental $/day (compute), recommended immediate action, hire window
Low-burst, +15%, +22.5M, $7,200/day, enable burst reserve + short-term spot-pools, N/A (monitor)
Sustained growth, +50%, +75M, $24,000/day, open 2 contract GPU slots + enable autoscale, 8-12 weeks
Shock (large customer), +200%, +300M, $96,000/day, emergency price-floor + prioritization + sales outreach, accelerate hiring and contractor pool, 12+ weeks
Latency regression (p95 > 160ms), N/A, N/A, SLA throttles per-route and soft-price bump (see triggers), investigate kernel/runtime config, expedite mitigations

Heuristic trigger matrix (first-pass):
- 0–20% uplift sustained >14d: finance monitor, enable burst reserve, no hires; adjust cost allocation to feature buckets.
- 20–60% uplift sustained >21d: open contractor slots (4–8 GPU-weeks), implement per-customer throttles, consider 8–12 week hire plan.
- >60% uplift sustained >14d or >30% uplift + latency regressions: surface to execs, initiate hiring pipeline for 2–4 FTEs (12+ week window), price-floor changes for new signups.
- Any single-customer causing >25% delta in daily tokens: calendarized sales + legal outreach; consider temporary quota/contract re-negotiation.

Price-sensitivity experiments (what to run):
1) Micro price-floor: raise new-customer price-floor by 8% for 30d in one region; measure churn and token delta per-account.
2) Soft throttles on non-PL1 routes: decrease max tokens/session by 10% for low-tier customers; track delta in usage vs revenue.
3) Burst-reserve purchase vs spot pools: simulate cost under +50% uplift for 30d to determine break-even for reserved capacity.

Sample quick calcs (editable sheet values):
- Incremental cost/day = incremental_tokens_per_day * token_cost
- Incremental headcount cost/day (amortized 12mo) = new_hires * (fully_loaded_cost/365)
- Price bump required to offset incremental cost = incremental_cost / daily_revenue

Operational playbook (short):
- Detection: finance on-call monitors 7d and 30d token deltas; automated alert at +20% 30d.
- Immediate: enable burst reserve and activate spot pool scaling; notify solutions_eng and customer_success for top-10 accounts.
- 48–72h: if uplift persists, open contractor requisition and schedule hiring pipeline planning (recruiter + hiring manager).
- 2–4 weeks: if sustained uplift, test micro price-floor changes (A/B regions) and quota-based throttles.
- >6 weeks: prioritize hiring and formal price changes for new contracts; update public quotas and docs.

Open questions / risks:
- How much elasticity do enterprise customers show with small price-floor changes? (need A/B)
- Can we automate per-customer prioritization quickly enough during shocks? (engineering effort estimate)
- What fraction of token mix is generators vs embeddings during bursts? (affects per-token cost)
- Vendor/GPU supply risk: how fast can Dedicated pools be expanded in APAC?

Next steps / TODOs:
- [ ] Wire up an A/B test for a 8% new-customer price-floor in us-west (owner: Ethan).
- [ ] Create a short contractor requisition template for 4–8 week GPU infra contractors (owner: Lena).
- [ ] Build a dashboard widget showing per-customer 30d token delta + contribution to daily cost (owner: Samir).
- [ ] Confirm amortized cost-per-hire assumptions with People Ops and update sheet.

Notes to self / rough thoughts:
- Prefer price-tier experiments on new signups only to reduce churn risk.
- Consider using caching/quantization pushes as a first cost lever before broad pricing changes; quantify unit-econ uplift per model quantization.
- Keep legal looped for any per-customer throttles; some contracts require 30d notice.

References and links:
- Confluence sim: confluence/FIN-ops/token-price-sim
- JIRA: JIRA-FIN-1234 (pricing A/B infra)
- Slack thread: #finance-ops; thread id p1234567890

Bottom line: put simple, actionable thresholds in the on-call playbook (alerts + 48h actions + 3-week hiring threshold + 90d pricing experiments). This doc is a pocket guide — move any formal simulation tables to the analytic workbook linked above.
